title: The induced character formula for the quotient model
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, $H\leq G$ a subgroup, and $W$ a finite-dimensional complex vector space with a linear $H$-action. Its character is $\chi_W(h)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf C}(h\mid W)$. Form $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G W$ by quotienting $\mathbf C[G]\otimes_{\mathbf C}W$ by $[xh]\otimes w=[x]\otimes hw$, with $a([x]\otimes w)=[ax]\otimes w$. For every $g\in G$, writing $C_G(g)=\{x\in G:xg=gx\}$ and $g^G=\{x^{-1}gx:x\in G\}$, one has
$$\chi_{\operatorname{Ind}_H^G W}(g)=\frac1{|H|}\sum_{x\in G,\;x^{-1}gx\in H}\chi_W(x^{-1}gx)=\frac{|C_G(g)|}{|H|}\sum_{h\in H\cap g^G}\chi_W(h).$$
Both fractions are interpreted in $\mathbf C$; the assertion includes $H=G$, $H=\{1\}$ and $W=0$. Finite-dimensionality is [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], and tensor and quotient modules are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. Trace is [def-weil-endomorphism-trace].

proof.text: Write $[x,w]$ for the class of $[x]\otimes w$ in the stated quotient $U$. Tensor generators span, and quotient surjectivity shows that the $[x,w]$ span $U$. They are linear in $w$ and satisfy $[xh,w]=[x,hw]$. Left multiplication by $a\in G$ sends the defining relation to $[axh,w]-[ax,hw]=0$, so it descends. On generators, $1[x,w]=[x,w]$ and $a(b[x,w])=(ab)[x,w]$; these also show that each action map is invertible, with inverse the action of $a^{-1}$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free], choose a basis $(b_i)_{i\in I}$ of $W$. It is finite: take a finite spanning family from [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] and let $I_0$ be the union of its finite basis supports. Every vector has support contained in $I_0$, whereas $b_i$ has support $\{i\}$, so $I=I_0$. Choose a set $S$ of representatives of the left cosets $G/H$. It is finite since $G$ is finite. Every $x\in G$ is uniquely $sh$ with $s\in S,h\in H$: equal cosets determine $s$, then cancellation determines $h$.

proof.text: Put $D=\bigoplus_{s\in S}W$, with inclusions $\iota_s$. Define $A:D\to U$ by $A((w_s))=\sum_s[s,w_s]$. Define a bilinear map on $\mathbf C[G]\times W$ by $([sh],w)\mapsto\iota_s(hw)$, extending linearly in the specified group-algebra basis. The tensor universal property gives a linear map on $\mathbf C[G]\otimes W$. For $h'\in H$ its values on $[shh']\otimes w$ and $[sh]\otimes h' w$ are $\iota_s((hh')w)$ and $\iota_s(h(h' w))$, which agree by the action law. It kills the span of all relations, so it gives $B:U\to D$ by $B([sh,w])=\iota_s(hw)$: two representatives of a quotient coset differ by a vector in that span and have the same image.

source.place: Agent-written auxiliary calculation for inherited Step 3 representation input; explicit maps between coset coordinates and the quotient. The blueprint does not contain this calculation; Serre Part I Chapter 7 is WANTED.

proof.text: For every $s,w$, $BA(\iota_s w)=\iota_s w$, and for every $x=sh,w$, $AB([sh,w])=[s,hw]=[sh,w]$. These spanning generators show $BA=1$ and $AB=1$. In $D$ the vectors $\iota_s b_i$ span by expansion in each coordinate; if a linear combination is zero, its $s$-coordinate is a zero combination of the $b_i$, forcing every coefficient to vanish. Thus $e_{s,i}=[s,b_i]$ is a basis of $U$. Its finite index set is $S\times I$, proving that the induced representation is finite-dimensional.

source.place: Agent-written auxiliary calculation for inherited Step 3 representation input; inverse checks and the exhibited basis of induction. The blueprint does not contain this calculation; Serre Part I Chapter 7 is WANTED.

proof.text:
Fix $g\in G$. Write $gs=t h$ uniquely with $t\in S,h\in H$. Then $g e_{s,i}=[gs,b_i]=[t,hb_i]$. If $t\ne s$, every coefficient in the $s$-block is zero. If $t=s$, equivalently $s^{-1}gs\in H$, the diagonal coefficients in this block are those of $s^{-1}gs$ on the basis $(b_i)$ of $W$. Summing diagonal entries, exactly the trace formula of [def-weil-endomorphism-trace], gives
$$\chi_U(g)=\sum_{s\in S:\ s^{-1}gs\in H}\chi_W(s^{-1}gs).$$

source.place: Agent-written auxiliary calculation for inherited Step 3 representation input; trace as the sum of diagonal matrix entries. The blueprint does not contain this calculation; Serre Part I Chapter 7 is WANTED.

proof.text: For $x=sh$ put $k=s^{-1}gs$. Then $x^{-1}gx=h^{-1}kh$, which belongs to $H$ exactly when $k\in H$. In that case the action matrices of $h^{-1}kh$ and $k$ on $W$ are conjugate by the invertible action matrix of $h$; basis independence and $\operatorname{tr}(PAP^{-1})=\operatorname{tr}(A)$ from [def-weil-endomorphism-trace] give equal characters. The bijection $S\times H\to G$, $(s,h)\mapsto sh$, therefore rewrites the sum over all $x$ with $x^{-1}gx\in H$ as $|H|$ times the sum in Step 5. The integer $|H|$ is positive because $1\in H$; its image in $\mathbf C$ is nonzero. Division proves the first equality.

proof.text:
For $k\in H\cap g^G$, choose $x_0\in G$ with $x_0^{-1}gx_0=k$. The map $C_G(g)\to\{x\in G:x^{-1}gx=k\}$, $c\mapsto cx_0$, is a bijection: $(cx_0)^{-1}g(cx_0)=x_0^{-1}gx_0$ when $cg=gc$; conversely, if $x^{-1}gx=k=x_0^{-1}gx_0$, then $c=xx_0^{-1}$ satisfies $c^{-1}gc=x_0x^{-1}gxx_0^{-1}=g$. Its inverse is $x\mapsto xx_0^{-1}$. Thus every such fibre has $|C_G(g)|$ elements. Partitioning the finite set $\{x:x^{-1}gx\in H\}$ by the value $k$ gives
$$\sum_{x:\ x^{-1}gx\in H}\chi_W(x^{-1}gx)=|C_G(g)|\sum_{k\in H\cap g^G}\chi_W(k).$$
Substitute into the first equality to obtain the second.

proof.text: No step requires positive dimension or a proper nontrivial subgroup. If $W=0$, its basis is empty, Step 4 gives $U=0$, and all traces and sums vanish. If $H=G$, take $S=\{1\}$, so Step 5 is $\chi_U(g)=\chi_W(g)$; Steps 6 and 7 still apply. If $H=\{1\}$, Step 5 is zero for $g\ne1$, since $s^{-1}gs=1$ would force $g=1$; for $g=1$ each of the $|G|$ blocks is the identity of $W$, giving $|G|\dim_{\mathbf C}W$. This also covers the trivial group and confirms the stated edge cases.
